issues.legal_issue: Payments made for a prospecting licence are capital receipts rather than revenue receipts when the licence grants a right to remove part of the mineral asset.
material_facts: The dispute arose from income-tax assessments of payments received for prospecting licences.
The licences authorized the licensees to enter the land, prospect for bauxite, and take away and appropriate samples in reasonable quantities.
The Court found that the right to remove samples amounted to a grant of a right to part of the licensor’s capital asset, not merely permission to use it.
The payments were made in consideration of the rights granted by the licences.
issues.conclusion: The payments were capital receipts and were not assessable to income tax; the appeal was allowed and the referred question was answered in favour of the assessee.
issues.legal_principle: The character of a receipt depends on the nature of the rights granted by the transaction. A payment for the realisation or transfer of a right to part of a capital asset is capital, whereas a payment merely for use of a capital asset may be revenue. The Court relied on Raja Bahadur Kamakshya Narain Singh of Ramgarh v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa (1943), which treated salami paid to acquire rights under a mining lease as capital; Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa v. Raja Bahadur Kamakshya Narain Singh (1946), concerning payments for prospecting and mining rights; and The Member for the Board of Agricultural Income Tax, Assam v. Smt. Sindurani Chaudhurani (1957), which described salami as a single, non-recurring payment made before creation of a tenancy and as consideration for the landlord parting with a right. It also considered The Province of Bihar v. Maharaja Pratap Udai Nath Sahi Deo of Ratugarh (1941), which stated that salami is not income where it cannot be regarded as rent paid in advance.

rule.if: income_tax_assessment_appeal and prospecting_license_granted and licensee_authorized_to_enter_and_prospect and licensee_authorized_to_remove_mineral_samples and payment_received_for_granted_right

predicates.income_tax_assessment_appeal: The dispute arose in an appeal concerning whether receipts assessed as income were taxable.
predicates.prospecting_license_granted: The licensor granted a licensee permission to prospect for minerals on land.
predicates.licensee_authorized_to_enter_and_prospec: The licensor authorized the licensee to enter the land and conduct prospecting operations.
predicates.licensee_authorized_to_remove_mineral_sa: The licensor authorized the licensee to take away and appropriate samples from the mineral deposit.
predicates.payment_received_for_granted_right: The licensor received payment in consideration of the rights granted under the licence.
predicates.receipt_is_capital_and_not_taxable: The payment is a capital receipt and is not taxable as income.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment appeal concerns payment for a prospecting licence that authorizes the licensee to remove mineral samples, the payment is treated as a capital receipt and is not taxable.
